title: staged-deploy-token-offset-decoding-regression-postmortem
summary: During a staged rollout of rw-v2-large-quant to a small canary pool, we observed a decoding regression manifested as repeated leading subtokens (BOS-like artifacts) and higher than expected token consumption for a subset of requests. The issue was limited to canary hosts running the new quantized weight bundle and only reproducible when requests hit the dynamic-batching path with batch size >= 4. Impact to production traffic was limited by canary percentage but surfaced to a small number of customers and internal smoke tests.
incident_timeline:
2024-03-12 09:03 UTC - Automated canary health check 'decode_quality' started failing for rw-v2-large-quant on pool eu-west-1-canary
2024-03-12 09:06 UTC - SRE oncall (Evan) paged by PagerDuty due to alarm: decode_error_rate > 0.7% for canary pool
2024-03-12 09:10 UTC - Correlation: increased per-request tokens and elevated latency on canary hosts. Internal smoke tests show repeated leading subtokens in outputs when batch_size >= 4.
2024-03-12 09:25 UTC - Canary traffic percentage frozen and new canary rollouts paused.
2024-03-12 09:35 UTC - Decision made to rollback canary routes to previous model variant (rw-v2-large-qat-202402) and flush prefix/KV caches on affected hosts.
2024-03-12 09:50 UTC - Rollback completed, immediate alarms cleared.
2024-03-12 10:30 UTC - Post-rollback monitoring showed no recurring errors; mitigation work started to diagnose root cause.
2024-03-13 14:00 UTC - Root cause hypothesis confirmed with model-serialization and runtime team tests.
2024-03-15 11:00 UTC - Postmortem draft created and shared with stakeholders.
impact: Low customer-facing impact due to canary scope (approx. 0.8% of traffic) but visible for internal canary checks and 3 customer requests flagged by CS. No data loss. Increased costs from wasted token generation on failing requests during the canary window. Temporary degradation of latency on canary hosts while error occurred.
detection: Detected by automated 'decode_quality' canary checks that run synthetic prompts through the model and compute token-level divergence metrics. PagerDuty alert fired when decode_error_rate crossed threshold (0.7%). Engineers also noticed unusual increase in average tokens per response in canary telemetry dashboards.
root_cause: A subtle mismatch between the weight serialization metadata written by the model-onboarding pipeline and the runtime kernel selection logic. The quantized bundle included a new 'embedding-layout' flag in the manifest that was intended to optimize memory layout; however, when present it triggered the runtime's alternate embedding-lookup kernel compiled for a different embedding table ordering. Under single-request paths the mismatch was masked by prefix caching; when requests were batched (batch_size >= 4) the alternate kernel's indexing produced repeated leading subtokens (off-by-one subtoken offsets) for a subset of sequences. The KV-cache TTL and automatic prefix caching interacted with partial cache hits, making the issue non-deterministic and harder to reproduce in unit tests.
immediate_mitigation: 1) Freeze canary rollout and pause any additional invitations to the canary pool. 2) Route new canary traffic away from the affected quantized variant. 3) Rollback canary hosts to previous validated model bundle. 4) Flush prefix/KV caches on affected hosts to avoid polluted partial-cached states. 5) Add temporary alarm to detect repeated leading subtokens and token-count anomalies at a lower threshold for accelerated detection.
mitigation_timeline:
2024-03-12 09:25 UTC - Canary freeze enacted.
2024-03-12 09:35 UTC - Rollback to rw-v2-large-qat-202402 started.
2024-03-12 09:50 UTC - Rollback complete, caches flushed.
2024-03-12 10:05 UTC - Lower-threshold anomaly alarm enabled.
2024-03-12 10:30 UTC - Monitoring confirmed alarm cleared and metrics returned to baseline.
follow_up_actions: Add embedding-layout manifest compatibility checks in model-onboarding to assert kernel selection invariants
Add integration test in runtime CI to run parity tokenization/decoding tests for both quantized and full-precision bundles across batch sizes 1-8
Update canary smoke test to include batched synthetic prompts that exercise KV-cache partial hits
Add checksum of embedding table ordering to weight signing process and reject bundles with unexpected ordering
Documented escalation path between model-onboarding and runtime teams when manifest flags are added
Create a lightweight fuzzer that sends randomized prefix histories and batch sizes to detect offset regressions before rollout
runbook_changes: Proposed edits to the model rollout runbook: 1) Add a 'batch parity' smoke test step that explicitly tests batch sizes 1-8 and both cold and warm KV-cache states. 2) During canary: increase sampling of customer-like prompts and enable the 'leading-subtoken' anomaly detector. 3) Add a checklist item to verify embedding-layout and kernel mapping metadata match expected runtime kernels. 4) Include a rollback checklist that includes cache flush and canary-percentage freeze commands.
monitoring_updates: New metrics added: 'leading_subtoken_rate', 'per_request_token_waste', and 'canary_decode_nll_divergence'. Dashboards created for quick triage; alerts added with two thresholds (warning and pager). Also instrumented per-model-bundle kernel-selection metric so we can correlate which kernel was chosen on each host.
owner_notes: Key takeaway: small changes to serialization metadata can have outsized, non-deterministic effects when combined with batching and caching. We should treat any manifest flag that affects memory/layout as high-risk and gate it behind parity tests. Coordination between model-onboarding and runtime is the immediate priority — moving forward we'll require a signed-off compatibility matrix for every new manifest flag.
